 ATP Finals 2026 live updates: Latest as Shelton takes on Zverev after Fils defeats Jodar on day three
 Follow live from the second round of matches at the ATP Finals in Turin today. Live Blog Chat The Athletic Live Team November 17, 2026 at 3:09 PM EST U.S. star Ben Shelton faces Alexander Zverev at the ATP Finals after Arthur Fils beat Rafael Jódar.   Getty Images Nancy Froston · Senior Writer, Live Shelton vs. Zverev: ATP Finals latest
 The ATP Finals continue with the third day of action in Turin, Italy today. 
 Alexander Zverev (1) is in action against U.S. star Ben Shelton (3) in the singles.
 How to watch: Tennis Channel (U.S.); Sky Sports (UK)
 Streaming: Tune in with Fubo (U.S. and Canada, try for free )
 Join the discussion here or email: live@theathletic.com 
 1 A. Zverev 0 5 3 B. Shelton Serving 15 1 LIVE 6 A. Fils 4 6 6 Winner 8 R. Jódar 6 2 2 Completed Tue, Nov 17 View all Tennis Matches SKIP ADVERTISEMENT Advertisement
 November 17, 2026 at 3:09 PM EST George Ramsay · Staff Writer, Live Zverev leads by a double break
   Getty Images Zverev (1) *4-1 Shelton (3) 
 And from having two break points of his own, Shelton soon finds himself facing three at 0-40. 
 A wide serve saves the first, then Zverev shanks a forehand for 30-40. 
 Can Shelton get to deuce? No — a forehand error sees Zverev go a double break ahead. 
 November 17, 2026 at 3:06 PM EST George Ramsay · Staff Writer, Live Two break points pass by for Shelton
 Zverev (1) 3-1* Shelton (3) 
 Better from Shelton. A crunching forehand return puts him 0-30 up on Zverev's serve, then he gets two break points when the German wafts a forehand wide. 
 Shelton goes after a second serve but finds the net, then Zverev shuts the door with an ace down the middle. 
 A netted backhand sees the German survive and remain a break ahead. 
 November 17, 2026 at 3:01 PM EST Nancy Froston · Senior Writer, Live Crucial hold for Shelton
   Getty Images This is a match up between two of the biggest servers in tennis right now — Shelton is very dangerous when he gets those first serves right.
 But Zverev is causing so many problems for the American when playing through the court despite a remarkable five aces for Shelton in that game. 
 A vital hold for him under immense pressure.
 November 17, 2026 at 2:58 PM EST George Ramsay · Staff Writer, Live Shelton saves break points
   Getty Images Zverev (1) *2-1 Shelton (3) 
 More trouble for Shelton on his serve. He leads 40-15 at 2-0 before ballooning two backhands long in a row for deuce. 
 Superb power from Zverev brings up another break point, but Shelton saves it with an ace. 
 A big forehand swiped out the middle of the court by the top seed then leads to break point number three of the set, but a couple of aces see Shelton escape. 
 And the American holds from there when Zverev's scooped lob goes long, finally getting him on the board. 
 November 17, 2026 at 2:51 PM EST George Ramsay · Staff Writer, Live Fast start from Zverev
 Zverev (1) 2-0* Shelton (3) 
 Zverev lands his second blow, rattling through his first service game to love.
 An ideal start for the German. 
 SKIP ADVERTISEMENT Advertisement
 November 17, 2026 at 2:48 PM EST George Ramsay · Staff Writer, Live Zverev breaks in the first game
   Getty Images Zverev (1) *1-0 Shelton (3) 
 A bit of pressure on Shelton's serve early on as he finds himself down 15-30, then sends a backhand just long to hand Zverev an early break point. 
 The American can't find a first serve, then goes into the net with his forehand to fall behind early on. 
 First blow to the world No. 1. 
 November 17, 2026 at 2:45 PM EST George Ramsay · Staff Writer, Live We're underway!
 Zverev (1) 0-0* Shelton (3) 
 Off we go! Shelton gets us underway in the Inalpi Arena. 
 November 17, 2026 at 2:43 PM EST George Ramsay · Staff Writer, Live If he does get his first win against Zverev tonight, then Shelton will be through to the semi-finals. 
 Zverev, meanwhile, needs to win in straight sets to guarantee his progress with a game to spare. 
 The warm-up is now over — we'll be underway very soon. 
 November 17, 2026 at 2:41 PM EST George Ramsay · Staff Writer, Live Shelton winless against Zverev
   Getty Images The head-to-head between these two makes pretty grim reading for Shelton — he's yet to win in six meetings with Zverev , collecting only two sets. One of those occasions was in this year's U.S. Open final.
 On the court, Zverev wins the toss and elects to receive. 
 November 17, 2026 at 2:36 PM EST George Ramsay · Staff Writer, Live The players are out on the court
 Here we go then! Time for the tennis to get back underway. 
 Alexander Zverev and Ben Shelton are out on the Inalpi Arena court for their second match of the tournament.

 November 17, 2026 at 2:33 PM EST Lukas Weese · Staff Writer, Live Shelton by the numbers
   Getty Images It’s been a fascinating season for Ben Shelton . He defended his title at the Canadian Open. He reached his first Slam final at the U.S. Open. 
 But he also lost 19 times this year. Here are the stats behind Shelton’s 2026 season, along with his career at the ATP Finals: 
 2026: 
 Grand Slams: 11-4
 Hard court: 32-12
 Overall: 46-19
 ATP Finals: 
 Career W-L: 1-3
 November 17, 2026 at 2:20 PM EST Nancy Froston · Senior Writer, Live A new face in Shelton's box
   Getty Images Ben Shelton has a new-look coaching team with the recent addition of Juan Carlos Ferrero , who recently coached Carlos Alcaraz to six of his seven Slams.
 Ferrero will work alongside Shelton’s current coach and dad, Bryan. 
 “Ben has extraordinary talent, power and character,” Ferrero wrote in a graphic published on Instagram.
 November 17, 2026 at 2:10 PM EST James Hansen · Senior Managing Editor, Tennis What is the prize money for the 2026 ATP Finals?
   Getty Images This year’s prize pool is $15.75 million. 
 It is allocated per match win and structured so the champions in singles and doubles take home the biggest prize if they go through the event undefeated with five wins (three round-robin wins, a semifinal win, and then victory in the final). 
 An undefeated singles champion will win $5.17 million. Last year’s prize pool was $15.5 million.
 The winner of the singles final will receive just over $2.4 million, while the winner of each semifinal will receive just over $1.2 million; the prize for a round-robin match win is $405,000 and each singles player receives $338,000 just for appearing at the event, provided they play all three of their round-robin matches.
 The winning doubles pair will receive $959,300 if they go undefeated.
 November 17, 2026 at 2:00 PM EST James Hansen · Senior Managing Editor, Tennis ICYMI: A reminder of the ATP field
   Getty Images At this year’s ATP Finals in Turin, Italy, a new world No. 1 is trying to fend off a resurgent generational talent — and the defending champion is nowhere to be found.
 Alexander Zverev goes into the season-ending event for the best eight singles players and doubles pairs of the year on top of the singles rankings, after winning two Grand Slam titles in 2026. 
 Snapping at his heels is Carlos Alcaraz , who returned from a right wrist injury at the U.S. Open and has won two tournaments in a row going into Turin. Missing is home hero Jannik Sinner, the biggest star in Italy and the two-time defending champion. 
 A right knee injury has kept Sinner off the court since his Wimbledon title this summer, and it’s his absence, alongside that of Alcaraz, in which Zverev has seized the top ranking.
 Joining Sinner and Alcaraz are four debutants, in the shape of Italy’s Flavio Cobolli, France’s Arthur Fils, Frances Tiafoe of the U.S. and Spain’s Rafael Jódar, who is the first man to reach the event in the same year that he made his ATP Tour debut.
 Ben Shelton of the U.S. and Russia’s Daniil Medvedev complete the field.
 November 17, 2026 at 1:49 PM EST Amelie Claydon · Sports Writer Context behind previous allegations against Zverev
 Brenda Patea was the second former girlfriend to accuse Alexander Zverev of domestic abuse. Olya Sharypova made allegations against him in 2020. 
 She did not pursue charges; a 15-month ATP Tour investigation found there was “insufficient evidence” to substantiate Sharypova’s allegations and Zverev did not face disciplinary action. Zverev called the allegations “unfounded and untrue.”
 Patea alleged that Zverev pushed her against a wall and choked her during an argument in 2020, which Zverev has always denied. She reported the incident to police in October 2021. Two years later, a criminal court in Berlin issued a penalty order of nearly $500,000 against Zverev. 
 Prosecutors can seek such orders if they believe that the evidence in a case is compelling enough that no trial is required. Zverev contested the order, and called it “complete bull****” during a news conference at the 2023 Paris Masters.
 The trial took place during the French Open, where Zverev reached the final, losing to Carlos Alcaraz. In a news conference, he said of the absence of a verdict:
 “That’s what dropping the case is. That is innocence. They’re not going to drop the case if you’re guilty at the end of the day. … I don’t know what translations you have, but that’s what it means.”
 As he prepared to give a runner-up speech at the 2025 Australian Open, a woman in the crowd shouted out in apparent reference to the allegations: “Australia believes Olya and Brenda! Australia believes Olya and Brenda!”
 “I believe there are no more accusations,” Zverev said in his news conference when asked about the incident. “There haven’t been for, what, nine months now. Good for her, I think she was the only one in the stadium who believed anything in that moment.”

 November 17, 2026 at 1:27 PM EST Amelie Claydon · Sports Writer Zverev to face lawsuit over alleged false statements on domestic abuse case
   Getty Images Alexander Zverev is set to face a new lawsuit over an alleged “false factual assertion” regarding the conclusion of a domestic abuse case against him.
 Brenda Patea, Zverev’s former partner and mother of his daughter, filed a civil lawsuit on September 18 seeking an injunction and financial compensation over comments Zverev made to French newspaper “L’Équipe” that Patea’s allegations of domestic abuse had “been proven false” and his “innocence had been proven.”
 The lawsuit centers on Zverev’s description of a 2024 criminal case that he and Patea settled out of court. 
 Legal proceedings were discontinued without a verdict determining guilt or innocence, and Zverev paid more than $218,000 split between legal costs and charity organizations. The terms of the settlement with Patea have not been disclosed.
 Patea alleges the remarks breached an agreement restricting public statements about their previous legal proceedings because, her lawsuit argues, it is not the case that Zverev was proven innocent. 
 “This is nothing more than an expression of opinion, protected by the freedom of speech,” Dr. Anna Sophie Heuchemer, a lawyer representing Zverev, told The Athletic by email. Heuchemer added that Zverev and his legal representatives would defend the case.
 November 17, 2026 at 1:04 PM EST James Hansen · Senior Managing Editor, Tennis Zverev ‘annoyed’ at having to explain No. 1 status
   Getty Images New world No. 1 Alexander Zverev lost his first match at the top of men’s tennis — and then expressed frustration with how his ascent has been received.
 “I feel like I’m the only world No. 1 in tennis history that has to explain why it’s OK for me to be world No. 1, which I find quite difficult, because I think I deserve to be where I am, even though I lost today,” Zverev said after a 7-6(5), 6-2 defeat to Italy’s Lorenzo Musetti at the Paris Masters.
 He described himself as having been “annoyed” by the reaction to his becoming the 30th man to reach the top spot since the introduction of computerized ATP Tour rankings in 1973.
 “I don’t think anybody had to explain themselves as much as I had to do in the last couple of days, which for me, is annoying, to be honest,” the German added.
 Zverev, 29, became world No. 1 earlier this month, overtaking Italy’s Jannik Sinner. He has won two Grand Slam titles in 2026, more than any other men’s player, taking the French Open and U.S. Open titles.
 November 17, 2026 at 12:40 PM EST Matthew Futterman · Senior Tennis Writer Being world No. 1 can get in a player’s head
   Getty Images Being the world No. 1 can get in a tennis player’s head. There are more questions to answer; there are more opinions to give.
 In Zverev ’s case, he has been asked a lot about his opinion on himself, and whether he feels like the best player in the world (he isn’t, and he knows that) and whether he deserves to be the world No. 1 (he does).
 Still, his central claim — that he has had to justify his ranking more than any other world No. 1 — requires some context.
 Thomas Muster was asked in 1996 about whether he was bothered by the criticism that came with being the world No. 1 at a time when Pete Sampras and Andre Agassi were the dominant players in the sport. 
 “I don’t give a s–––, honestly,” Muster said at Indian Wells that March, when asked whether criticism from fellow players about him and the rankings system bothered him.
 Zverev went 3-9 against top-10 opponents before the ATP Finals this season. He hasn’t beaten Djokovic, Alcaraz, or Sinner all year. That’s not entirely his fault since Alcaraz and Sinner have both missed roughly half the season with injuries. 
 He’s played 84 matches this season and won 66 of them. But all the times he has faced Alcaraz, Sinner or Djokovic, he has lost. He has still had the best season of anyone in the sport. 
 That’s why he’s the world No.1, even if he is essentially the world’s third-best tennis player, and why he deserves the ranking. Just like Muster did, even when he wasn't necessarily the best player on the planet either.
 November 17, 2026 at 12:08 PM EST James Hansen · Senior Managing Editor, Tennis Context behind Zverev's rise
   Getty Images Zverev has won 66 matches this year, and is 63-9 against opponents ranked 11 and below, but he is 4-9 against top-10 players.
 From the 2024 Australian Open to this year’s Australian Open, Sinner and Alcaraz won nine consecutive majors between them, Alcaraz five and Sinner four. Since then, both have missed long periods due to injury.
 In their absence Zverev has seized the opportunity to reach the summit, winning his first two majors along the way. At the start of 2026, he was almost 7,000 rankings points behind Alcaraz, 23, and almost 6,500 behind Sinner, 25. 
 Before the start of the ATP Finals, he had a 3,000-point cushion to Alcaraz at No. 3, while sitting narrowly ahead of Sinner, who is world No. 2. His ascent has also been polarizing in other ways. 
 He has been accused of domestic abuse by two different former partners, allegations which Zverev has always strenuously denied. Now he has the prize he sought. But he is not quite as happy as he expected.
